constraints: DELIVERABLE ZERO — the duplication audit. Before writing any proposal, read every one of the 19 listed proposals and write duplication_audit.md recording: the glob you executed, the file count returned, and a one-line statement of what each existing proposal already covers. Every new proposal carries a `discriminated_from` block naming the NEAREST existing IDEA and stating the concrete observable, object, or quantifier that differs. 'Different framing' is not a discrimination. If you cannot name a differing observable, do not file the proposal.

Object-first per docs/inventor-protocol.md: name the tracked object, apply the lossy-projection test, and specify the null-object control that would show the object carries no information. A proposal with no null object is incomplete.

Every proposal carries `heuristic_assumptions` (each with an experimental validation route) and `target_complexity` (time and memory exponents versus the best known). Do not soften a conditional claim into an unconditional one.
Mint every IDEA id with `python3 tools/allocate_id.py --next idea --date 20260806` and confirm with `--check` before writing the file. Never grep for the next free number (AGENTS.md rule 14).

PRIMARY SOURCES ARE UNREACHABLE from this environment (eprint, arXiv, NIST are blocked). You therefore may not label any idea's novelty stronger than `unverified`, and you may not dismiss an idea as known either. Where you hold an unverified recollection, label it exactly that.

GOAL-SSI-001's own record states p^{1/3+o(1)} is the tight classical exponent with 12 sub-p^{1/3} avenues closed by named structural obstructions (DEC-20260805-596d71). An idea that reopens one of those 12 must name the obstruction it claims to route around and say why the obstruction does not apply. Ideas that do not target the exponent must be honest that they are cost-model or measurement work.
Write ONLY under your write_scope. Never overwrite an existing proposal file. Do not create hypothesis records, do not approve anything, do not commit.
Never fabricate a citation, a measurement, a run, or a record ID (AGENTS.md rule 9). If a number is not in a committed artifact you can name, it does not go in a proposal.

tasks.title: Freeze EXP-SSI-697354: the Wesolowski crossover curve p*(w) as an executable contract

handoff.objective: Convert IDEA-20260803-48e258 into a specified hypothesis H-SSI-7fe2bf and a FROZEN, approved experiment contract EXP-SSI-697354 that an Executor can run in this environment with no new compute and no unavailable dependency.
inputs: EV-SSI-59f7a2 (concrete cost 2^{118.5}-2^{123} at SQIsign NIST-I; red-team SLIGHTLY UNDERSTATED; memory 2^{92.5} entries)
EV-WESO-b6ceff and KN-FIND-4e7a92 (corrected seam-free estimator; the 47 committed margin numbers)
constraints: THE CONTRACT MUST BE EXECUTABLE HERE. SageMath and g6k are ABSENT; numpy is present. The whole point of selecting this proposal is that it is arithmetic on already-committed numbers. If the design needs a dependency that is not installed, you have designed the wrong experiment — redesign it, do not schedule an infrastructure request.

The deliverable object is a CURVE, not a number: p*(w), the prime size at which the corrected p^{1/3+o(1)} method overtakes Delfs-Galbraith, as a function of available memory w. Specify the exact input table (which committed file, which columns, how many rows), the exact cost functions on both sides, and the exact crossover-solving procedure.

MANDATORY CONTROLS. (1) A reproduction gate: the contract must recover EV-SSI-59f7a2's committed 2^{118.5}-2^{123} bracket at the parameters where that record evaluated it, or the run is invalid. (2) A null-object control: evaluate the same procedure with the corrected estimator replaced by the SUPERSEDED one and show the curve moves — a procedure that returns the same curve either way is measuring nothing. (3) A monotonicity check on w that could actually fail.

Declare the claim tier explicitly. This is a COST-MODEL result on an extrapolated estimator, not an executed attack: it may not assert that SQIsign is broken, weakened, or that any parameter set is unsafe. State the affected-vs-safe scope, with NIST-III/V explicitly noted as retaining margin under every tested overhead scenario.

The hypothesis record must state mechanism, predictions with metrics, test boundary, and falsification criteria (AGENTS.md rule 2). The contract must state controls, metrics, budgets, stopping rules, and required artifacts BEFORE execution (rule 3).

Carry IDEA-20260803-48e258's uncertainty forward honestly: the record says the SIGN of the margin is robust and the MAGNITUDE is not. A contract that produces a single confident curve without a band contradicts its own input.
This task SPECIFIES and APPROVES a contract. It runs nothing, changes no goal status, and promotes nothing to knowledge/. Do not commit.
Use the pre-allocated ids H-SSI-7fe2bf and EXP-SSI-697354 exactly; both were --check confirmed free at batch open.

tasks.title: Red-team the SSI proposals and the frozen contract

handoff.objective: Attack this batch on two fronts: are the new proposals actually new and actually falsifiable, and can the frozen contract EXP-SSI-697354 produce a result that survives its own controls?
inputs: The 19 pre-existing SSI/SSIQ proposals named in the ideation handoff
constraints: Independent session. You did not produce these artifacts and you do not repair them.

DUPLICATION IS THE PRIMARY ATTACK. For each new proposal, independently check the nearest-neighbour claim: open the proposal it says it is discriminated from AND at least two others you pick yourself. A proposal that restates an existing one in new vocabulary is a finding, not a contribution.

CONTROL-CANNOT-FAIL IS THE SECOND ATTACK (KN-TECH-1a5b7e). For every control in EXP-SSI-697354 and every null object in the new proposals, state whether it is capable of returning a negative. This campaign's own record contains 33 consecutive batches of controls that all passed because none could fail — that is the failure mode to hunt.

Check the contract against AGENTS.md rules 5 and 7 and docs/claims-and-verification.md: does anything in it license a security claim about SQIsign that a cost-model extrapolation cannot support? Does it present a toy or extrapolated quantity as crypto-scale validation?
Verify the contract's dependency claim yourself. If it needs anything beyond numpy, say so — an unrunnable contract is a defect at design time, not an infrastructure problem later.
Name the single cheapest observation that would falsify the top-ranked new proposal, and the single cheapest that would invalidate the contract's output.
You write objections. You do not change status, do not edit raw artifacts, and do not commit.
